_note: Starter task keys for the sample department. Replace with tasks written for the real department before the pilot, and run validate_against_department first. Briefs are grids, forms, logs and email extracts, never the sentences a participant should produce. Each task carries 7-8 intended constraints: at 1-3 a participant's error rate could only land on 0, 0.33, 0.67 or 1.0, which is coarser than the 5-percentage-point non-inferiority margin.

tasks.title: Your own teaching week
brief: You are Dr. Sarah Lee (L001). You teach CS101 (Introduction to Programming, 45 students) and CS101L (Programming Lab, 45 students).
WEEK GRID, shaded cells: the whole of Friday is shaded solid.
Wednesday periods 4, 5 and 6 are shaded in a lighter tone. Key: 'lighter = would rather avoid'.
Margin note on the grid: 'earliest acceptable start: period 2'.
Margin note: 'Tuesday and Thursday suit me best'.
Margin note: 'three periods in a row is my limit - any more and I cannot do it'.
ROOM BOOKING SLIP, pre-filled: CS101 -> Lecture Theatre 1 (R101). Marked 'confirmed, do not change'.
EQUIPMENT FORM for CS101L: '45 networked workstations'.
Post-it on the two course cards: 'same day if you can manage it'.

intended.source_text: [task T1] Tuesday and Thursday suit me best
[task T1] three in a row is my limit
[task T1] same day if you can manage it

tasks.notes: The hard/soft split is carried by the shading key and by 'cannot' against 'would rather' and 'if you can manage it'. Nothing here is phrased as a constraint sentence.

COMPLAINTS LOG: 'Several asked not to be timetabled in period 1. Would help if we could avoid it.'
EQUIPMENT FORM for CS202L: '38 networked workstations'.
ROOM BOOKING SLIP, pre-filled: CS201 -> Lecture Theatre 2 (R102). Marked 'confirmed'.
Post-it on the CS202 and CS202L cards: 'students prefer these together on one day'.
LEAVE FORM, Dr. James Okafor (L004): 'unavailable Monday period 1, standing commitment'.

tasks.notes: Reported speech, so the cue words sit inside quotations. 'Would help' and 'though we got through it' mark the soft ones.

tasks.title: Department administrator
brief: You are setting the department-wide rules.
POLICY EXTRACT, clause 4.1: 'No class may be timetabled in period 1. This applies to every course without exception.'
ROOM INVENTORY: R101 Lecture Theatre 1 seats 120; R102 Lecture Theatre 2 seats 60; R301 Seminar Room 1 seats 30 (seminar).
ROOM BOOKING SLIP: CS301 (Machine Learning, 25 students) -> R101. Marked 'confirmed'.
ROOM BOOKING SLIP: CS302 (Final Year Project Seminar, 25 students) -> R301. Marked 'confirmed'.
ENROLMENT EXTRACT: CS301 and CS302 are both taken by Year 3 Group A (G3A). Registry flag: 'overlap would block attendance'.
LEAVE FORM, Dr. Mei Tan (L003): 'Fridays, all day, for the whole semester'.
WORKLOAD NOTE, Prof. Ahmad Rahman (L002): 'contract caps continuous teaching at 3 periods'.
PREFERENCE FORM, Ms. Priya Nair (L005): ticked 'Tuesday' under 'days I would prefer'.
TIMETABLER'S NOTE: 'CS101 and CS102 are different cohorts, so an overlap is survivable, but we would rather keep them apart.'

intended.source_text: [task T3] survivable but would rather keep apart

tasks.notes: Tests department-wide scope (both subjects null on no_early_start) and the same type appearing once hard and once soft, which the strength rules have to separate.

tasks.title: An email thread
brief: An email thread has arrived. Work out what can be timetabled.
Prof. Ahmad Rahman (L002): 'I am on the examinations board every Thursday this semester. I cannot teach then.'
Ms. Priya Nair (L005): 'Could you keep my teaching to two days a week?'
Year 1 tutor: 'Please avoid period 6 for the first years (G1A) - they are exhausted by then.'
Dr. Sarah Lee (L001): 'Mornings suit me best, the first three periods.'
Registry: 'CS302 is a seminar and needs a seminar room. Any one will do.'
Year 1 tutor: 'G1A should not sit through more than four periods in a row, ideally.'
Year 1 tutor: 'CS101 and CS102 on the same day would suit both cohorts, if it works out.'
Registry: 'No class before period 2 for Year 1 Group B (G1B). Transport arrives late.'

intended.note: Caps the number of distinct teaching days per lecturer. No frozen type expresses a count of days.
Excludes one specific late period. no_early_start sets an earliest period only, so no frozen type expresses this.

intended.source_text: [task T4] not more than four, ideally
[task T4] same day would suit, if it works out

tasks.notes: Two of the eight cannot be expressed in the frozen vocabulary. Recognising that is the correct answer; forcing them into a near-fitting type scores wrong_type, which is the finding. The email voice means cues arrive as 'cannot', 'ideally', 'if it works out' and 'needs'.
